pairs.subject: docs-content-model
pairs.evidence: scripts/docs/check-adrs.mjs:245 These gates read internal engineering markdown files from disk (a directory walk plus front-matter parse), so the subject's precondition is missing: there is no typed category/topic/body catalog in the app's module graph serving a published docs surface. Searching scripts/ and app/ for topicCatalog, bodyMap, watchedSources, checkedAgainst and isTopicVisible found nothing; the record/index and sources checks that do exist are a lint over a file-based corpus, which belongs to the knowledge-vault and docs-synchronization subjects.

techniques.evidence: scripts/docs/check-adrs.mjs:216 A record-to-index bijection check exists, but it compares a hand-maintained markdown index with ADR files on disk. There is no typed topic table or body map for it to guard. This is the file-substrate lint the golden path hands to knowledge-vault.

scripts/docs/api-reference.mjs:14 The API reference is generated from route files, not from a docs catalog, so there is no nav, sequence or count projection to judge. The 'not a second list' spirit is there, but it is aimed at routes, not topics.

scripts/docs/check-adrs.mjs:13 ADR front matter has `sources:` and `date`, which look like watched-sources and review-date fields. But they are frontmatter on files, read by a drift gate, and the golden path assigns that gate to docs-synchronization. There is no typed topic record with optional fields whose absence carries a declared meaning.
scripts/docs/check-adrs.mjs:27 This is a decision-lifecycle vocabulary for internal ADRs. Nothing gets published, so there is no visibility predicate or build-time flag for draft topics to gate.

scripts/docs/check-doc-sync.mjs:22 The feature-doc-map couples source globs to doc files so a change-boundary drift hook can use it. That is docs-sync stewardship, not a typed product-area handle on a topic record.
